result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.symmetric_difference()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the symmetric difference of this graph and another graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12435-L12500){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.symmetric_difference(other) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns a new graph containing edges that are in exactly one of the two graphs. Equivalent to `(G1 - G2) ∪ (G2 - G1)`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph to compare with. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph containing edges in exactly one of the graphs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graphs have different directedness. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Symmetric difference keeps edges present in exactly one of the two graphs, dropping any node that ends up edge-isolated. Unlike `difference()` it is symmetric: the same set comes back regardless of which graph makes the call. Both operands must agree on directedness. This is the go-to operation for surveying all changes between two network snapshots without having to reason about direction. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Edges `1-2` and `2-3` are shared by both graphs and drop out, leaving only the triangle's closing edge `3-1`, which exists in just one of them: ::: {#662ae954 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Triangle g1 = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(1, 4): g1.add_node() g1.add_edge(1, 2) g1.add_edge(2, 3) g1.add_edge(3, 1) # Path g2 = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(1, 4): g2.add_node() g2.add_edge(1, 2) g2.add_edge(2, 3) sym_diff = g1.symmetric_difference(g2) sym_diff.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Unlike `difference()`, this is symmetric, which makes it well-suited for spotting everything that changed between two network snapshots, regardless of which direction the change went.
